overview: This House resolution set the ground rules for debating two measures. It allowed the House to take up H.R. 5371, a stopgap spending bill (called a continuing resolution) to keep the federal government funded at the start of the 2026 budget year, with one hour of debate and no amendments beyond one motion to send it back to committee. It also scheduled debate on H. Res. 719, a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Charlie Kirk. In addition, it changed a date in an earlier rules resolution, H. Res. 707, from March 31, 2026, to January 31, 2026. The House adopted the resolution, with the final procedural step taken on September 17, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution allowed the House to move quickly on a bill to prevent a government shutdown before the budget year began.
against: Critics say limiting debate and blocking amendments kept members from offering changes to a major spending bill.
